messages:
Emma (CS): MiraTravel reported 403s to the Redwood API right after our scheduled network maintenance at 00:00 UTC. They say their allowlist no longer matches our egress IPs. Ticket #7529 attached logs and the customer is blocked in prod.
Ryan (Oncall): Ack — assigning. Any evidence this is a config rollback or cloud NAT change?
Emma (CS): Customer noted the client IP seen in their firewall logs changed at 00:03. They sent this sample curl response from their side: `curl -v https://api.redwood.ai/v1/health` -> TLS handshake ok, 403 body `access_denied`.
Lee (NetOps): I see a maintenance job ran: network/nat-pool-rotate — cloud provider rotated the NAT gateway and propagated a new set of egress IPs. Deploy-bot posted the rotation at 00:01:03.
deploy-bot: Automated maintenance: nat-pool-rotate completed (pool-id: np-43, new-ips assigned).
Ryan (Oncall): Can we reproduce from our private VPC instance? Need quick repro steps to share with MiraTravel so they can update allowlist or we can offer a workaround.
Lee (NetOps): Running quick checks from a test instance in the same region:``` 
# from bastion
$ curl -s https://ifconfig.me
198.51.100.27
$ dig +short myip.opendns.com @resolver1.opendns.com
198.51.100.27
```
Lee (NetOps): Their allowlist contains 198.51.100.12 and 198.51.100.13 (old pool). New egress is 198.51.100.27. That explains the 403s.
Emma (CS): Customer asked if we 'rolled' their IPs without notice — they require static egress for allowlist.
Ryan (Oncall): Short-term options: 1) Provide MiraTravel the new IPs to whitelist, 2) Offer temporary tunnel to our dedicated egress pool (if they accept shared egress), 3) Roll back the NAT change for their tenant if on Dedicated/Private. Which is feasible?
Lee (NetOps): We can add a safety mapping for their dedicated VPC to use the previous NAT allocation for 24 hours while they update allowlist. I'll open a rollback patch: `netops rollback-nat --tenant mira-travel --from np-43 --to np-41 --window 24h`.
Emma (CS): I'll send the new IPs plus rollback option to MiraTravel and ask for confirmation which they want.
support-bot: Ticket updated: rollback request queued (REQ-9876). Ops will take action after approval.
MiraTravel (via CS): Please do rollback, we will whitelist the new range in the morning.
Ryan (Oncall): Proceeding with rollback now. I'll monitor for residual 403s and TTL/propagation issues.
Lee (NetOps): Rollback applied at 00:20 UTC. Confirmed test calls from MiraTravel's confirmed source are succeeding.
Emma (CS): Customer confirmed success at 00:28, says API calls are back to normal. They requested a postmortem and clearer notice next time.
Ryan (Oncall): Action items: - NetOps to add option to pin a static egress CIDR per tenant (P1). - CS to update docs with guidance for allowlisting dynamic pools + recommended CIDR ranges. - Infra to add an email/webhook notify list for scheduled NAT rotations.
Lee (NetOps): Filed infra ticket INFRA-2145 for per-tenant egress pinning.
Emma (CS): I'll close the customer ticket once we share the summary. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
Ryan (Oncall): Marking this thread resolved. Reminder: check rotation playbook to include explicit customer-facing notifications for affected tenants.
summary: MiraTravel production API 403s after scheduled NAT pool rotation changed egress IPs. NetOps rolled back to previous NAT for the tenant while customer updated allowlist. Follow-ups: per-tenant static egress option, improved notifications, KB update.
